286227922_6139dc6b.text: In rodents, the core of the thalamus is almost entirely composed of glutamatergic excitatory neurons. (O'Reilly et al., 2020) These glutamatergic nuclei are surrounded by a shell of GABAergic neurons, corresponding essentially to the thalamic reticular nucleus (TRN). The TRN is organized in sectors that are specifically and reciprocally connected to the different thalamic nuclei. Because the TRN contains only inhibitory neurons, it is considered the main modulator of the core nuclei's excitability. (Cox et al., 1997)(Murata et al., 2018) For instance, the TRN controls the flow of information delivered to the cortex and regulates the dynamics of the thalamocortical dialogue during the different vigilance states (active, quiet wake, and sleep). (Crunelli et al., 2018)

286227922_659e1ccf.text: humans, inhibitory neurons can be found in most core thalamic nuclei, but the TRN remains the main source of inhibition to the core nuclei.
